matchstick.title: Single‑stick numeral reduction
matchstick.principle: A numeral that differs from another by exactly one stick can be altered by moving that stick while keeping the character valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single numeral is off by one stick and can become a correct numeral by moving that stick.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a numeral and leaving the source numeral without a valid shape.

matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their original orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical stick and vice versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever moving a stick, ensure its orientation matches the target character’s required orientation.
matchstick.example: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical stick when forming an I.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick must be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, enforce that the total number of sticks stays constant.
matchstick.example: Adding an extra stick to a numeral or deleting a stick without relocating it.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every numeral and operator must still be a legal Roman numeral or allowed operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate move, check that all symbols remain valid.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: The transformed equation must be mathematically true; compute the numeric values of both sides to ensure equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a transformation, evaluate the arithmetic before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Swapping ‘=’ and ‘‑’ operators without checking that the resulting equality holds.

matchstick.title: Operator swap via stick exchange
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred from one operator to another, changing both symbols while preserving orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is close and swapping ‘+’, ‘‑’, or ‘=’ might balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to ‘‑’, turning them into ‘‑’ and ‘=’, but not verifying the new equality.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: Removing a stick from an X or a V leaves a single diagonal line, which is not a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Never remove a diagonal from X or V unless you also add a stick to keep the character valid.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from V to use elsewhere, leaving V as a single diagonal line.

matchstick.title: Cross‑numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved from one numeral to another, potentially changing both values, as long as each resulting character remains a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When adjusting the values of two numerals simultaneously can balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to another numeral, leaving the source I empty.

matchstick.title: Track stick orientation counts
matchstick.principle: The numbers of vertical, horizontal, and diagonal sticks must be unchanged after the move; count them to catch hidden errors.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After a candidate move, verify that the total count of each stick orientation remains the same.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick to a place that requires a horizontal orientation, altering the orientation count.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be moved to a different position within the same numeral, preserving its orientation, to transform the numeral into another valid Roman numeral (e.g., V → X by moving one diagonal).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is nearly correct but a single numeral is off by shape, consider repositioning one of its own sticks rather than moving it between characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from one arm of a V so that the two diagonals cross, turning the V into an X while leaving the rest of the equation unchanged.

matchstick.description: Rotating sticks (treating a diagonal as vertical or vice‑versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model conflates stick orientation when moving sticks, assuming any stick can be reoriented.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce that a stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) must stay the same after relocation.

matchstick.description: Adding or removing sticks instead of moving exactly one
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes creates or deletes sticks while trying to adjust numerals or operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count sticks before and after a move; the total must remain unchanged.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid numerals after a move
matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick can leave a character with a shape that does not correspond to any Roman numeral or allowed operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every character matches a known valid Roman numeral or operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may focus on making a syntactically valid equation without checking the numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after a transformation and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.description: Changing operators to disallowed symbols (e.g., turning ‘=’ into ‘≠’)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes interprets a stick move as creating a non‑allowed operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Restrict operator transformations to the allowed set {+, -, =} and ensure the resulting symbol is valid.
